To

We will do the same here.
When we look in the mirror we are

They appear to be coming from

We can get this point by extending the rays backwards as shown

The image does not really exist the way we see in other cases,

This image that we get by extending the rays backwards is called a
virtual image.
We cannot get this on a screen like a real image.

peculiar properties of concave mirrors.
They enlarge the image when the

in shaving mirrors and mirrors used by dentists.
Another property is the

1.3 Ray Diagrams: (Image formation by convex mirror)
One can draw ray diagrams for a convex mirror too.
The ‘easy’ rays
that we identified earlier can be used in this case with small modification.
Here there are three rules which describe these rays.
The procedure for

Rule 1: A ray parallel to the axis, on meeting the
convex mirror will get reflected so as to appear as if it
is coming from the focal point.
See fig.-17.
Rule 2: This is
converse of Rule 1.
A
ray travelling in the
direction of the focal point, after
reflection, will become parallel to the
axis.
See fig.-18.
Rule 3: A ray travelling in the direction of the
centre of curvature will, on reflection, travel in the
opposite direction and appears to be coming from the
centre of curvature.

parsed_output.answer: We prefer a convex mirror as a rear-view mirror in vehicles because it provides a wider field of view. This is due to the fact that convex mirrors diverge the light rays, making the image appear smaller but covering a larger area. As a result, the driver can see more of the traffic behind, which helps in avoiding accidents. Convex mirrors also form virtual, erect, and diminished images, which are always visible in the mirror but cannot be projected on a screen.

required_point_details.point: A convex mirror forms a virtual, erect, diminished image
It provides a wider field of view
Therefore a driver can see a larger region behind the vehicle

unsupported_claims: A convex rear-view mirror forms a real image on a screen
